Please try again.') and three curl variants return HTTP 401 {"error":"invalid_credentials"} for test@test.com with the exact password 'Q#s%EbEuj#nzB93JIfmnfafZ' from /app/memory/test_credentials.md and the review request (verified same backend accepts tracktest.ap3p customer login = 200 + token, so proxy + auth endpoint are healthy). This is either (a) the staff password was rotated / never deployed to the production WP user 'dan' (WP user id 17), (b) the staff account is not approved on prod WP, or (c) a WP app-password change not reflected in test_credentials.md.

rca_of_issue: CRITICAL staff login failure RCA. Symptom: production POST /api/glp/auth/session with {email:'test@test.com', password:'Q#s%EbEuj#nzB93JIfmnfafZ'} returns 401 {"error":"invalid_credentials"}. Reproduction (verified 4 ways): (1) Playwright page.fill() + login-submit -> login-error 'Something went wrong. Please try again.'; (2) curl --resolve app.ap3p-fitness.com:443:35.214.14.95 with Content-Type: application/json and literal body -> 401; (3) curl with %25-escaped password -> 401; (4) curl with \u0025 JSON-escaped password -> 401. Control: the same POST with customer tracktest.ap3p@mailinator.com / TrackTest2026! returns 200 with a token, proving the proxy, GLP connector v2.1.4 and WP wp_authenticate pipeline are healthy. Therefore the issue is NOT an encoding bug on # or % — the production WP user record for test@test.com simply does not have the password 'Q#s%EbEuj#nzB93JIfmnfafZ' set. Mitigation: on production WP (ap3p-fitness.com), set/rotate the password or Application Password for user id 17 'dan' (role glp_fulfilment) to 'Q#s%EbEuj#nzB93JIfmnfafZ', OR update /app/memory/test_credentials.md with the current production staff credentials. No frontend/code change required.
